name: Fellow
tagline: Agendas, notes, action items, recordings, and meeting analytics

pricing.basis: paid plan; billing basis requires review
pricing.native: Public paid plan exists; amount not safely recovered
pricing.notes: The official pricing URL is recorded, but a stable current amount was not safely recoverable in this pass. Do not publish a number until rechecked.

tiers.name: Free
tiers.limits: Maximum 5 seats; 5 AI notes lifetime per user and 5 AI recordings lifetime per user.

tiers.name: Team
tiers.limits: Maximum 20 seats; 10 AI notes per user/month and 10 AI recordings per user.
tiers.notes: The public card does not append a time period to the 10-recording limit.

tiers.name: Business
tiers.limits: Maximum 50 seats; unlimited AI notes and recordings.

tiers.name: Enterprise
tiers.limits: Starts at 10 users; unlimited seats, AI notes, and recordings.
tiers.notes: Annual price is public; monthly price is not.

pricing.freeTierCaps: Up to 5 seats; each user gets 5 AI notes lifetime and 5 AI recordings lifetime.
pricing.billingTerms: monthly + annual; Enterprise starts at 10 users and publishes annual pricing only
pricing.hiddenCosts: Enterprise has a 10-seat minimum, and the lower plans have hard workspace caps of 20 and 50 seats.

verdictSummary: The visible meeting management loop is buildable, but a credible replacement needs more than the first screen. Fellow earns its keep through capture, integrations, reliability, so expect a weekend or multi-day build and a narrower personal scope.
coreLoopDIY: Build a private meeting management pipeline that accepts an audio file, transcribes it, creates structured notes, and exports Markdown.
replacementScope: narrow personal or very small-team substitute
requirements: local Whisper model or optional API key in .env
whyPeopleStillPay: Fellow: Customers pay for automatic capture, dependable speaker handling, search across calls, and notes arriving without manual file wrangling.
ongoingBurden: Own audio capture permissions, diarization quality, model downloads, storage, privacy, and integrations.

priorArt.name: whisper.cpp
priorArt.desc: Local speech-to-text engine suitable for private transcription.

rejectedAlternatives.name: Meetily
rejectedAlternatives.desc: Records and summarizes meetings, but has no shared agenda system or meeting analytics.

rejectedAlternatives.name: Speakr
rejectedAlternatives.desc: A searchable transcript workspace, not a meeting-management system with agendas and recurring rituals.

notes: Useful boundary case: the first 60 percent of Fellow is approachable, but operating the last 40 percent is the real subscription.
prompt:
Build a deliberately narrow personal substitute for Fellow, not a full clone.
Use exactly this stack: Python 3.12 + FastAPI + whisper.cpp + SQLite.
Primary job: Build a private meeting management pipeline that accepts an audio file, transcribes it, creates structured notes, and exports Markdown.
Start from an empty folder and create the complete working project.
Make the default mode single-user and private.
Store user data locally unless the core job requires the declared self-hosted database.
Do not add analytics, telemetry, ads, or third-party accounts.
Put every secret and external credential in .env and provide .env.example.
Use realistic sample data that is clearly labelled and easy to delete.
Implement the smallest polished interface that completes the core loop end to end.
Include clear empty, loading, validation, success, and failure states.
Add import and export so the user is not trapped in the app.
Use accessible keyboard navigation, labels, focus states, and sensible contrast.
Validate untrusted input and never log secrets or private file contents.
Deliberately exclude these paid-product advantages: live multi-speaker accuracy; calendar and CRM integrations; cross-call team analytics.
Do not fake integrations, network effects, proprietary data, model quality, compliance, or security claims.
Where an external API is optional, keep the app useful without it and explain the degraded mode.
Write focused unit tests for the data model and the most important workflow.
Add one end-to-end smoke test that proves the core loop works.
Create a README with setup, permissions, architecture, data location, backup, and limitations.
Add scripts for install, development, test, build, and a production-style local run.
Run the tests and build before finishing, then fix errors rather than merely describing them.
